scope: Fix one exceptional object for the two cumulative endpoints of the actual identity-form Proposition 9.2 call and compose all twelve positive terms in the final published Bordignon Theorem 1.4. Do not perform psi-to-prime-count transfer, density normalization, common-cutoff absorption, or threshold calculation.

literature_search.principle: Use the final published theorem and its proof before adding a project bridge; compare version, quantifiers, endpoint convention, center, and every positive remainder term.
searched_sources: Bordignon 2021 final NYJM Theorems 1.1-1.4 and proof equations (34)-(37)
FGKMT 2018 Theorem 6 and Section 8 actual identity-form call
literature_search.limitation: The targeted search is not a worldwide nonexistence or novelty claim. The X0/Y0 notation discrepancy remains unresolved.

observed_version_differences: The arXiv v1 theorem centers the discrepancy at u/phi(q), whereas the final NYJM theorem uses psi(u)/phi(q).
The final NYJM C-term and first E-term have different log factors from the v1 source.
Only the final NYJM statement and final proof equations (34)-(37) are used in this contract.

actual_variable_map.common_small_modulus_cut: Q1=(log T)^A, fixed while Theorem 1.4 is applied at u=T and u=2T

common_exceptional_object.bordignon_quantifier: For a fixed Q1, q0 denotes the exceptional modulus up to Q1 if it exists.
common_exceptional_object.selection: If q0 exists, choose one prime divisor B of q0; otherwise set B=1.
common_exceptional_object.filter_implication: (q,B)=1 implies q0 does not divide q.
common_exceptional_object.maynard_subset_relation: The Maynard family q<=T^(1/3),(q,B)=1 is a subset of each Bordignon non-exceptional family q<=Q_B(u,A),q0 not dividing q.
common_exceptional_object.size: B<=q0<=Q1<=Q_B(T,A)<sqrt(T)<T for T>1; B is 1 or prime and satisfies both FGKMT Lemma 7.2's B<=T condition and Maynard's actual alpha=2 condition.
common_exceptional_object.coefficient_coprimality: The selected identity form has leading coefficient 1, hence it is coprime to B.
common_exceptional_object.scale_dependence: This chooses one B for each fixed outer scale X and its dyadic pair, as allowed by Hypothesis 1; it does not construct one global B for every X.

published_final_remainder.normalization: Each listed formula is the corresponding positive RHS term R_j(u)/u. Write L=log u, ell=log L, delta=1/(2*A*R1*ell), and lambda=log Q1.

bordignon_constant_normalization_caution.observation: Theorem 1.2 defines C(alpha1,alpha2,Y0) with Y0=log log X0, while final Theorem 1.4 and proof equation (35) print C(A,A-3,X0).
bordignon_constant_normalization_caution.implementation_rule: The evaluator accepts theorem12_constant_upper as an explicit input and does not invent or silently reinterpret it.

next_gate.description: Convert the open-closed cumulative von Mangoldt interval bound to Maynard's exact half-open unweighted identity-prime count, retaining endpoint atoms, prime powers, partial summation, and the exact centered total.
next_gate.then: H1c-1b.4 bounds the full twelve-term remainder and represented-prime density by one common finite cutoff.
